description:
The build script produces the packaged tree in the build output directory from the repository files the manifest declares as live sources, and the result is proven equal to the checked-in tree that still ships.

## Background

The workflow package is embedded into the binary as a whole directory at compile time, so every asset an adopter receives has to exist inside that directory. This repository consumes the same files at their working paths, which is why sixty-one asset pairs are carried twice in the tree. Producing the packaged tree at build time is what removes the second copy, and it is the piece that has to work before anything can depend on it.

Two properties of the build output directory make this more than a copy loop. It is not reset between builds, so a live consumer that is deleted or renamed leaves its copy behind unless the run reconciles the subtree it owns. And rewriting it unconditionally moves timestamps on every run, which relinks every test target — the regression an earlier change removed from this build script by making it read nothing ambient — so a destination is written only when its bytes differ from its source.

The checked-in copies are still in place while this lands, and that is the point: with both trees present, the produced tree can be compared against the one it will replace, file for file. That comparison is a direct observation rather than a claim made after the originals are gone, and it is the evidence that the later re-rooting is safe.

Ordering is guaranteed rather than arranged: the build script runs to completion before the rest of the package compiles, so whatever reads the tree later always reads a finished one.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The build script produces the package tree under the build output directory from the repository files the manifest declares as live sources.
- [hard] REQ-02: The build script re-runs when a file beneath any declared live root changes, and when the manifest changes.
- [hard] REQ-03: A declared live source absent from the repository fails the build with a message naming the path.
- [hard] REQ-04: The build script writes a destination only when its bytes differ from the source it is produced from.
- [hard] REQ-05: The build script removes a file in the subtree it owns that the manifest no longer declares.
- [hard] REQ-06: The produced tree carries the same set of live-asset sources at the same package-relative paths, one for one with the checked-in tree, and each of those assets' bytes and executable declaration and repository target matches.
- [hard] REQ-07: That comparison runs while both trees exist, so it observes the equality directly rather than inferring it.
- [hard] REQ-08: The binary still embeds the checked-in tree, so nothing depends on the produced one until it is proven equal.

## Notes

The build script reads the manifest for the asset paths it produces and the roots it watches; it performs no manifest validation, which stays with the runtime package model that already rejects a declared-but-absent source and an undeclared package file.
title: Assemble the packaged tree at build time
